Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the methodology, cost assumptions and market data used in determining the grant thresholds of €95,000 for one residential unit, €115,000 for two units, and €135,000 for three or more units under the croí cónaithe Vacant Above the Shop Grant; if the adequacy of these thresholds has been reviewed in light of current construction, refurbishment, conservation and fire safety costs, particularly in Dublin city centre; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [39305/26]

questions.heading: Departmental Schemes
questions.question: 688. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the reason commercial properties held through company ownership structures are excluded from eligibility under the croí cónaithe above the shop scheme; if his Department has examined the extent to which this eligibility restriction may affect uptake of the scheme, particularly in Dublin city where many commercial premises are company owned; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [39306/26]

questions.heading: Departmental Schemes
questions.question: 689. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage if his Department has undertaken a review of the operation, uptake and effectiveness of the croí cónaithe above the shop scheme; if barriers to participation, including ownership structure requirements and refurbishment costs, have been identified as factors affecting application levels; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [39307/26]

questions.heading: Departmental Schemes
questions.question: 690. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of enquiries, applications, approvals, refusals and completed projects recorded by each local authority under the croí cónaithe above the shop scheme since its establishment; the total value of grants approved and paid in each case, in tabular form. [39308/26]

questions.heading: International Protection
questions.question: 780. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration the specific supports and protections that will remain available for vulnerable beneficiaries of temporary protection, including persons with disabilities, older persons, families with young children and those unable to access independent accommodation, in the event of any phased withdrawal of State-funded accommodation supports; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [38762/26]

questions.heading: Visa Agreements
questions.question: 781. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration further to Parliamentary Question No. 858 of 12 May 2026, the number of visa applications submitted by Palestinian nationals which were approved and refused in each of the past five years, broken down by applicants residing in Gaza, the West Bank, Lebanon and any other relevant location, where such data is available, in tabular form; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [38781/26]

questions.heading: Visa Agreements
questions.question: 782. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Justice, Home Affairs and Migration further to Parliamentary Question No. 858 of 12 may 2026, the reasons for the increase in visa application refusals involving Palestinian nationals in 2026 compared with each of the previous five years; whether any changes in policy, security assessments, documentation requirements, processing procedures or country specific considerations contributed to this increase; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [38782/26]

questions.heading: Departmental Policies
questions.question: 1066. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Children, Disability and Equality whether consideration has been given to the development of accessibility guidance or universal design standards for reverse vending machines and similar public service infrastructure to ensure independent access for persons with disabilities; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [40216/26]

questions.heading: Third Level Education
questions.question: 299. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science the further and higher education courses, programmes and access pathways currently available for persons with intellectual disabilities across universities, technological universities, colleges of further education and other State funded education providers; the number of places available in each institution and programme, in tabular form; the educational, personal and progression supports available to students participating in these programmes; the measures being taken by his Department to expand inclusive further and higher education opportunities for persons with intellectual disabilities; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [40535/26]

questions.heading: Third Level Education
questions.question: 300. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science whether his Department has assessed the geographical gaps in further and higher education opportunities for persons with intellectual disabilities, particularly in areas where no dedicated inclusive programmes currently exist; the steps being taken to improve regional access for students and families; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [40536/26]

questions.heading: Third Level Education
questions.question: 301. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Further and Higher Education, Research, Innovation and Science the funding currently provided to universities, technological universities and further education providers to support students with intellectual disabilities and additional needs; whether additional funding or targeted expansion measures are being considered to increase the number of places and supports available; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [40537/26]

questions.heading: National Development Plan
questions.question: 72. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Public Expenditure, Infrastructure, Public Service Reform and Digitalisation whether additional capital investment under the National Development Plan is being considered to support critical infrastructure needs in north Dublin, including rail capacity improvements, coastal flood protection and climate resilience projects in areas vulnerable to coastal overtopping and severe weather events; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [40812/26]

questions.heading: Special Educational Needs
questions.question: 91. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Education and Youth if she is aware of the increasing pressure on schools due to the growing number of students requiring additional care and educational supports; whether her Department is satisfied that current special needs assistant allocations are meeting the needs of students and schools; the steps being taken to increase the number of SNAs available, particularly in schools experiencing significant demand; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [40810/26]

questions.heading: Schools Building Projects
questions.question: 109. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Education and Youth the expected timeline for the evaluation of tenders and commencement of construction for the permanent school building project at a location (details supplied); whether her Department anticipates any risks to the currently envisaged late Quarter 3 2026 construction commencement date; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [40811/26]

questions.heading: School Staff
questions.question: 364. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Education and Youth if she will review the decision to reduce the mainstream teaching allocation for a school (details supplied) for the 2026-2027 school year; if she will consider allowing the school to retain its current teaching post in light of the likely impact on class sizes and educational supports; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [41323/26]

questions.heading: School Enrolments
questions.question: 365. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Education and Youth the number of parents or guardians required to complete forms or applications relating to children leaving school at age 16 in each of the past five years, despite the majority of young people now remaining in second-level education until age 18 or 19; whether consideration has been given to extending supports such as child benefit until age 19 in line with current educational participation; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [41324/26]

questions.heading: Healthcare Infrastructure Provision
questions.question: 509. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Health the current status of the capital approval and funding process for the redevelopment of the emergency department and wider capacity expansion project at Beaumont Hospital; whether the project remains within the National Development Plan capital pipeline; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [40813/26]

questions.question: 153. [43724/26]

questions.heading: National Security
questions.question: 174. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Defence the preparations that have been undertaken by her Department and the Defence Forces in advance of Ireland assuming the Presidency of the Council of the European Union; the additional personnel, funding, training, equipment and logistical resources being provided to support the security, ceremonial and operational requirements associated with the Presidency; whether contingency arrangements have been put in place; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [43723/26]

questions.heading: Road Network
questions.question: 453. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport whether his Department has examined the need for improved national coordination frameworks between utility providers and road authorities in relation to the scheduling and carrying out of road excavation works; whether consideration is being given to the development of national guidance, shared mapping systems or coordinated planning mechanisms to reduce repeated excavations of recently completed roads and footpaths; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [42596/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 480. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport whether the National Transport Authority or Iarnród Éireann has undertaken any assessment of passenger demand on DART services during bank holiday weekends and bank holiday Mondays over the past three years; if so, if he will provide the findings of such assessments, in tabular form; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43075/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 481. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport whether consideration has been given to operating enhanced DART frequencies on bank holiday Mondays during periods of high visitor numbers, favourable weather conditions or major public events; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43076/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 482. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport the passenger numbers recorded on DART services on each bank holiday Monday in 2025 and 2026 to date, compared with the equivalent average Sunday and weekday passenger numbers, in tabular form; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43077/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 483. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport whether any analysis has been undertaken of overcrowding levels on DART services serving coastal destinations including Clontarf Road, Killester, Raheny, Harmonstown, Howth Junction, Sutton and Howth during bank holiday weekends; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43078/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 484. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport whether he is satisfied that the current Sunday timetable operated on bank holiday Mondays adequately reflects travel demand patterns in the greater Dublin area; whether any review of this policy is planned; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43079/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 485. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport the number of occasions since January 2024 on which additional DART services were operated on bank holiday weekends due to increased passenger demand; the routes and dates involved, in tabular form; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43080/26]

questions.heading: National Transport Authority
questions.question: 486. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Transport whether the National Transport Authority has considered the introduction of a dedicated bank holiday timetable for DART services, distinct from the current Sunday timetable, in recognition of changing travel patterns and increased leisure and tourism demand; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [43081/26]

questions.heading: Artificial Intelligence
questions.question: 535. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether his Department has undertaken scenario modelling or fiscal risk assessments regarding the potential long-term impact of artificial intelligence and automation on corporation tax revenues, particularly in light of the State's reliance on multinational corporation tax receipts; whether assessments have been made regarding possible impacts on employment related tax revenues and taxable corporate profits in sectors exposed to automation; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [41950/26]

questions.heading: Artificial Intelligence
questions.question: 536. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether Government has undertaken any cross-departmental assessment regarding the potential long-term economic and labour market impacts of artificial intelligence and automation, including possible effects on employment levels, taxation receipts and economic stability; whether sectors particularly exposed to technological disruption have been identified; and the whole-of-Government measures that are being considered to support economic resilience and workforce adaptation in response to technological change. [41951/26]

questions.heading: European Union
questions.question: 557. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether his Department has engaged at EU level regarding the VAT treatment of sunscreen products; whether consideration has been given to seeking amendments at EU level to permit reduced or zero VAT rates for sunscreen products as preventative health items; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [42669/26]

questions.question: 558. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Tánaiste and Minister for Finance whether his Department has undertaken any assessment of the implications of the current VAT treatment of sunscreen products in the context of public health policy and skin cancer prevention; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [42670/26]

questions.heading: Artificial Intelligence
questions.question: 684. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Enterprise, Tourism and Employment whether his Department has assessed the potential labour market implications of artificial intelligence and automation for sectors with significant multinational employment concentrations; the measures that are being considered to support workforce adaptation, skills diversification and employment resilience in sectors exposed to technological disruption; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [41952/26]

questions.question: 696. [42675/26]

questions.question: 91. Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Education and Youth if she is aware of the increasing pressure on schools due to the growing number of students requiring additional care and educational supports; whether her Department is satisfied that current special needs assistant allocations are meeting the needs of students and schools; the steps being taken to increase the number of SNAs available, particularly in schools experiencing significant demand; and if she will make a statement on the matter. [40810/26]
